_comment: U12's frontend half: the gate that decides whether the application is mounted.
None of these mutations produces a broken-looking UI. The two that matter most produce a
*more convenient* one - the app renders straight away, which is exactly what a developer
would want and exactly what the backend then refuses. The rest turn a security property
into a cosmetic one: a masked password field that is not masked, an error message that
helpfully says which half of the credentials was wrong.
Note the frontend cannot grant access on its own - the API refuses regardless. What it can
do is show a login form to a single-tenant install that has no accounts, leak a username's
existence, or mount components that then fire authenticated requests while signed out.

mutations.name: config_answer_ignored
mutations.why: the order of the two questions is the whole design: without the config check, a single-tenant install - the default - gets a login form for an account system it does not have

mutations.name: session_asked_before_config
mutations.old:
setState({ status: "ready", enabled: false, user: null });
        return;
mutations.new: setState({ status: "ready", enabled: false, user: null });
mutations.why: falling through to the session request on a deployment with no accounts asks a question whose 401 answer means nothing, and the state it then sets contradicts the one just set

mutations.name: app_mounted_while_signed_out
mutations.why: a 200 with `user: null` would mount the app with nobody signed in, and every component below would immediately fire requests the API refuses

mutations.name: signed_out_renders_the_app_anyway
mutations.why: a 401 from the session endpoint is the normal signed-out answer; treating it as success mounts the app for an anonymous visitor

mutations.name: unreachable_server_looks_like_being_signed_out
mutations.why: the config endpoint needs no credentials, so a failure there is the backend being down - showing a login form blames the user for it and their correct password will not work

mutations.name: sign_out_does_not_sign_out
mutations.old:
setState({ status: "signed-out", enabled: true, user: null });
  }, []);
mutations.why: the server ends the session and the screen keeps showing the app, which on the shared machine that logging out is for is the whole risk

mutations.name: sign_out_abandoned_when_the_request_fails
mutations.why: a failed logout must still clear the screen; leaving the app up because the network blipped is the opposite of what was asked for

mutations.name: login_error_replaced_with_our_own_wording
mutations.new: setError("That user does not exist or the password was wrong.");
mutations.why: the API deliberately answers identically for a wrong password, an unknown username and a disabled account; inventing a message here is where username enumeration comes back

mutations.name: password_not_masked
mutations.why: shoulder-surfing is the threat this input type exists for, and the field still works perfectly without it

mutations.name: password_kept_after_a_failed_attempt
mutations.why: a failed password left in the field is a password left on screen, and it invites hammering the same wrong value into the rate limit
